notes.text: Marathi shares Devanagari with Hindi but adds a letter, La, and keeps a third gender: neuter, for things.
Namaskar fits any hour. Friends skip it and ask kay challay, what is going on, or in villages, Ram Ram.
Marathi has two words for we. Amhi leaves you out, aapan includes you, so choose carefully when introducing.
Four words for aunt and uncle: kaka and atya on your father's side, mama and mavshi on your mother's.
Varan is plain dal, amti the spiced one. Jevlas ka, have you eaten, is asked as a greeting.
Nineteen is ekonis, one less than twenty. Marathi counts down to every ninth number: ekonchalis is thirty nine.
Colours bend to gender: tambda shirt, tambdi sari, tambde phool. The word for red changes ending three ways.
The state bus is called lal dabba, red box. Ghat, a mountain pass, is the Marathi word English borrowed.
Hindi lets kal mean yesterday and tomorrow. Marathi splits them: kal is only yesterday, udya is only tomorrow.
Kay bhav ahe asks the rate. Bhav also means worth, which is why bhav khane means to act important.
Bara means both fine and recovered. Say mala bare vatat nahi, it does not feel good to me.
Ghar is the building; gharchi mandali, the house people, means your family. Ask about the house, you ask about them.
Kaam is any task, naukri the salaried kind. Ask kay karta and people answer with a job, not a day.
You never like something here. Mala aavadte means it pleases me, so feelings arrive at you instead of being owned.
Ganpati was a household ritual until Tilak took it to the streets in 1893, so people could gather where meetings were banned.
